independence_statement: Derived independently from the frozen Malachi strategy and exactly the 55 Mal.* WEB translation-witness rows. OSHB and UXLC Malachi files were used only to corroborate paragraph/form metadata. No active or archived Malachi chunk or review, other specialist proposal, boss artifact, global sidecar, M1-M6 map, comparison synthesis, or T417 layer was read.
authority_guard: This is candidate literary analysis only. It selects no canon, witness, translation, theology, fulfillment, identity, authorship, chronology, marriage law, covenant system, or eschatological reading. Paragraph markers and later-reused wording are evidence, never authority.

source_pins.use: source identity and line locators only

versification_note: WEB has chapter cardinalities 14, 17, 18, and 6. MT/WLC has 14, 17, and 24, so WEB Mal.4.1-4.6 maps to MT/WLC Mal.3.19-3.24. This crosswalk is translation-versification metadata, not a seam.

mandatory_parents.title: Priestly dishonor, offering pollution, command, covenant comparison, and consequence
mandatory_parents.hydration_rule: Retrieving Mal-LIT-002, Mal-LIT-003, or Mal-LIT-004 must expose this full parent and the adjacent priestly movements.
mandatory_parents.basis: Direct priestly address, despised-name language, threatened curse, covenant-of-Levi comparison, and public consequence form one indictment despite the real command seam at 2:1.

mandatory_parents.title: Command to priests measured by the covenant of Levi
mandatory_parents.hydration_rule: Mal-LIT-003 and Mal-LIT-004 are dependent siblings; retrieving either requires the complete parent.
mandatory_parents.basis: The sanctions in 2:1-4 state their covenant-with-Levi purpose, which 2:5-9 develops as ideal, reversal, and consequence.

mandatory_parents.title: Two coordinated covenant-treachery accusations
mandatory_parents.hydration_rule: Mal-LIT-005 and Mal-LIT-006 are dependent siblings; retrieving either requires the full parent.
mandatory_parents.basis: Repeated covenant and treachery language joins the communal accusation to the wife-of-youth dispute despite the paragraph after 2:12.

mandatory_parents.title: Harsh-words protest answered by fearers and the coming-day contrast
mandatory_parents.hydration_rule: Mal-LIT-009 and Mal-LIT-010 are dependent siblings; retrieving either requires protest, counter-scene, discernment, and outcome.
mandatory_parents.basis: The proud and wicked in the protest are the contrasted groups whose outcome the day oracle supplies; the paragraph after 3:18 supports a child seam, not disconnection.

route.title: Heading hydrated with the love-and-Edom disputation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Mal.1.1 identifies revelation and addressees; 1:2 immediately opens the first-person love claim and quoted objection, while 1:5 supplies the recognition close and 1:6 changes to father/master questions addressed to priests.
route.rationale: The heading is not useful standalone literary speech, so it is hydrated with the full claim-objection-evidence-counterclaim-result movement. Israel's seeing-and-saying response closes the dispute before the new priestly vocative.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.1.1 alone: metadata without the revelation's first rhetorical act.
Mal.1.2-Mal.1.4: omits the audience-recognition result in 1:5.
Mal.1.1-Mal.1.6: 1:6 replaces the love objection with a new honor accusation.
counterevidence: A superscription can be catalogued independently.
Edom's speech in 1:4 creates an internal counterclaim turn.
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate 1:1 to decide whether Malachi is a name or office, or 1:2-3 to settle love/hate language apart from the dispute and recognition close.

route.title: Priests despise the great King's name through polluted offerings
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Father/master questions address priests in 1:6; quoted objections, defective offerings, governor comparison, altar refusal, nations contrast, renewed table accusation, curse, and great-King formula run through 1:14 before the explicit command onset at 2:1.
route.rationale: Accusation and objection in 1:6-7, evidence in 1:8-9, refusal and contrast in 1:10-11, renewed accusation in 1:12-13, and curse plus royal-name close in 1:14 form one escalating dispute.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.1.6-9 | 1.10-14: the latter applies the same polluted-table and name charge.
Mal.1.6-13 | 1.14: the curse and great-King reason resolve the offering accusation.
Mal.1.6-2.9 as one surface: 2:1 supports dependent priestly movements under the larger parent.
counterevidence: Mal.1.10 changes from entreaty to altar refusal and 1:11 broadens to the nations.
WLC-family samekh after MT 1:13 supports a real internal seam before 1:14.
evidence_refs: OSHB/UXLC paragraph metadata: samekh after MT Mal.1.13
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate 1:11 as a tense, worship, or nations proof text, or 1:14 as a detached curse; both operate inside the offering dispute.

route.title: Command to priests and threatened covenant sanctions
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Mal.2.1 announces a command; listen-and-honor conditions, curse, rebuke, humiliation, and recognition purpose run through 2:4, which names the covenant before 2:5 begins its idealized description.
route.rationale: The condition and sanctions belong with their stated covenant purpose in 2:4. The move at 2:5 from threatened second-person consequences to retrospective covenant description supports a dependent child seam with mandatory hydration.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.2.1 alone: announced command without content.
Mal.2.1-3: omits the sanctions' recognition and covenant purpose.
Mal.2.1-9 as the only surface: the command and comparison are retrievable children when their parent is preserved.
counterevidence: Mal.2.4 bridges forward by naming the covenant described in 2:5.
The full 2:1-9 movement shares priestly addressees and purpose.
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate 2:3 to settle offspring-or-seed wording or ritual imagery; retain command, conditional warning, and covenant purpose.

route.title: Levi ideal contrasted with corrupt priests
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Mal.2.5-7 describes reverence, truthful instruction, uprightness, and priestly knowledge; 'But you' in 2:8 reverses the ideal, and 'Therefore' in 2:9 gives the consequence before communal questions in 2:10.
route.rationale: Ideal, failure, and consequence form one antithetical comparison. Ending after 2:9 honors the paragraph marker and new communal voice without severing the standard from the accusation.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.2.5-7 | 2.8-9: the adversative failure depends on the ideal.
Mal.2.5-8: omits the 'Therefore' consequence.
Mal.2.5-10: 2:10 broadens from priests to communal brotherhood.
counterevidence: The adversative at 2:8 is a strong internal turn.
The priestly maxim in 2:7 has independent cataloguing value.
evidence_refs: OSHB/UXLC paragraph metadata: pe after MT Mal.2.9
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate 2:7 to define priestly or messenger identity without the Levi ideal, present reversal, and judicial consequence.

route.title: Communal covenant treachery and foreign-god accusation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: First-person-plural father, creator, brother, and covenant questions open at 2:10; 2:11 names Judah's profanation and 2:12 pronounces removal, followed by a paragraph and 'This again' at 2:13.
route.rationale: Questions, specified violation, and cut-off sentence form a compact accusation-result unit. The renewed offense at 2:13 supports a dependent sibling under the full treachery parent.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.2.10 alone: questions without accusation and sentence.
Mal.2.10-11: omits the consequence in 2:12.
Mal.2.10-16 only: paragraph and 'This again' support two hydrated children.
counterevidence: Covenant and treachery vocabulary binds this unit to 2:13-16.
The difficult paired expression in 2:12 lowers internal syntactic certainty.
evidence_refs: OSHB/UXLC paragraph metadata: pe after MT Mal.2.12
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate the father/creator questions or foreign-god idiom to decide referents, identity, ethnicity, or marriage law apart from the communal accusation.

route.title: Altar tears answered by the wife-of-youth covenant accusation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: 'This again you do' begins rejected altar lament; the quoted 'Why?' receives a covenant-witness accusation, and 2:15-16 repeat treachery admonitions before a paragraph and the new justice complaint.
route.rationale: The tears require the objection and explanation in 2:14, while the compressed 2:15 and repeated guard in 2:16 continue the admonitory close. Translation pressure is recorded without deciding marriage law.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.2.13 alone: complaint without reason.
Mal.2.13-14 | 2.15-16: repeated wife, spirit, and treachery language keeps the close attached.
Mal.2.13-17: 2:17 opens a different objection answered in chapter 3.
counterevidence: Mal.2.15-16 has severe translation and clause-division pressure.
Repeated treachery ties backward to 2:10-12.
evidence_refs: OSHB/UXLC paragraph metadata: samekh after MT Mal.2.16
route.proof_text_guard: Do not detach 2:15-16 to settle Spirit, offspring, hate, divorce, garment, violence, or marriage law; expose the whole dispute and translation pressure.

route.title: Justice complaint answered by messenger, refining, restored worship, and judgment
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Mal.2.17 asks where the God of justice is; 3:1 answers with preparation and sudden coming, 3:2-4 unfolds refining and restored offerings, and 3:5 promises near judgment before 3:6 turns to unchanging preservation and return.
route.rationale: The cross-chapter chain is explicit: complaint, coming answer, endurance questions, purification, restored worship, and swift witness. Neither the WEB chapter edge nor identity pressure in 3:1 outranks the complete rhetorical answer.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.2.17 alone: unanswered complaint.
Mal.3.1 alone: onset of the answer, not a self-contained identity oracle.
Mal.3.1-4: omits the judgment that answers the complaint.
Mal.2.17-3.4 | 3.5: purification and judgment coordinate as one answer.
counterevidence: The WEB chapter edge is a strong navigation convention.
Mal.3.5 broadens from priestly purification to social judgment.
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate 3:1 to choose messenger identities or fulfillment, or 3:5 as a detached social list; retain complaint and complete answer.

route.title: Return summons concretized in the tithe dispute and blessing result
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: Mal.3.6 grounds survival in unchanging commitment; 3:7 summons return and asks how, 3:8-9 answers with robbery, 3:10-11 gives remedy and reversal, and 3:12 closes with nations' recognition before a paragraph and new charge.
route.rationale: The general return objection at 3:7 is incomplete without the concrete answer at 3:8. Accusation, curse, command, test, blessing, crop protection, and nations coda form one dispute.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.3.6-7 | 3.8-12: the tithe accusation answers 'How shall we return?'.
Mal.3.8-10: omits crop protection and nations result.
Mal.3.6 alone: the claim grounds the return summons.
counterevidence: Mal.3.8 starts a fresh rhetorical question and objection.
Mal.3.10 has high independent retrieval value.
evidence_refs: OSHB/UXLC paragraph metadata: samekh after MT Mal.3.12
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate 3:6 as an abstract proposition or 3:10 as a detached financial promise; retain return, accusation, command, agricultural result, and coda.

route.title: Harsh-words protest countered by the fearers' response and discernment promise
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The harsh-words objection and service-profit claim run through 3:15; 'Then' shifts to fearers, divine hearing, memory, possession, sparing, and discernment through 3:18 before the causal day oracle.
route.rationale: The fearers' scene is enacted counterevidence to the protest: honored service, divine attention, possession, and discernment answer the claim that service has no profit. The paragraph supports a dependent day-oracle seam under the larger parent.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.3.13-15 | 3.16-18 as independent units: the counter-scene answers the protest.
Mal.3.13-17: omits the discernment result.
Mal.3.13-4.3 as the only surface: paragraph and 'For behold' support a hydrated child.
counterevidence: 'Then those who feared' is a clear internal scene change.
Samekh after MT 3:18 supports the surface close.
evidence_refs: OSHB/UXLC paragraph metadata: samekh after MT Mal.3.18
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate the memory book or treasured possession to decide heavenly record, remnant identity, or salvation; retain protest, counter-scene, and discernment.

route.title: Coming day distinguishes the proud from those who fear the name
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: 'For behold' opens the burning-day outcome; 'But to you who fear my name' gives the healing counterpart, and 4:3 completes reversal before the remembrance command in 4:4.
route.rationale: The destructive and healing panels form one balanced day oracle. It answers the preceding discernment dispute as a dependent child, while 4:4 changes to imperative remembrance and the coda.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.4.1 alone: only one half of the contrast.
Mal.4.2-3 separately: healing, leaping, and treading complete the same day.
Mal.3.13-4.3 only: paragraph supports dependent retrieval with parent hydration.
Mal.4.1-4: remembrance begins the coda.
counterevidence: WEB chapter edge and WLC-family paragraph reinforce retrievability.
Causal opening and repeated proud/wicked/fear vocabulary bind backward.
evidence_refs: OSHB/UXLC paragraph metadata: samekh after MT Mal.3.18 and pe after MT Mal.3.21/WEB Mal.4.3
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate furnace, sun-of-righteousness, healing-wings, or trampling images to determine sequence or identity; preserve both panels and the parent dispute.

route.title: Moses remembrance and Elijah sending form the reconciliation coda
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: After the pe at WEB 4:3, 4:4 commands remembrance of Moses; 'Behold, I will send' adds Elijah before the day, and 4:6 supplies heart-turning purpose and curse-risk close.
route.rationale: Moses remembrance and Elijah sending are paired book-level instructions: commanded teaching, anticipated reconciliation, and the final risk belong together. The onset at 4:5 is internal coordination, not permission to detach the final threat.
rejected_alternatives: Mal.4.4 | 4.5-6 as independent units: the named figures form a paired coda.
Mal.4.5 alone: sending requires purpose and consequence.
Mal.4.6 alone: the final curse is a negative purpose clause.
Mal.4.1-6: paragraph and imperative distinguish coda from day oracle.
counterevidence: Mal.4.5 has a fresh 'Behold' and distinct sending prediction.
Later reuse creates independent retrieval pressure but cannot govern the local seam.
evidence_refs: OSHB/UXLC paragraph metadata: pe after MT Mal.3.21/WEB Mal.4.3
route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate Moses, Elijah, the day, kinship turning, or final herem/curse to settle identity, fulfillment, family structure, canon order, or eschatology.

coverage_evidence.validation_method: Expanded every inclusive route span against WEB chapter cardinalities and compared the ordered sequence to the exact 55 filtered Malachi witness coordinates, requiring one occurrence of each coordinate.

hardest_seams.reason: Samekh makes the seam real, but curse and great-King reason close the charge.

hardest_seams.resolution: Dependent 2:1-4 and 2:5-9 children under 2:1-9 and 1:6-2:9 parents.
hardest_seams.reason: 2:4 completes sanction purpose and bridges to covenant description.
Paragraph and 'This again' support a seam; repeated covenant/treachery forbids disconnection.

hardest_seams.resolution: Reject the WEB chapter edge; keep 2:17-3:5.
hardest_seams.reason: Messenger, refining, restored offerings, and judgment answer the complaint.
The tithe accusation concretely answers 'How shall we return?'.
Paragraph and causal onset support retrieval; the day supplies the discernment outcome.

hardest_seams.resolution: Keep remembrance and sending as one coda.
hardest_seams.reason: Separate onsets are balanced closing instructions and the final purpose cannot be detached.

proof_text_policy: Every dependent child must expose its mandatory parent and siblings. No heading, quotation, priestly maxim, difficult marriage clause, messenger line, tithe command, memory-book phrase, day image, Moses command, Elijah sending, or final curse may be surfaced as a smaller authoritative unit.
review_note: No hold is proposed because tied retrieval treatments are resolved through mandatory parent hydration rather than denial of internal seams. A later reviewer may hold a treatment only with a precise answerable question and argued alternatives.
